property_summary: If initialization has not been called, calling SetMinSum(n) sets MinSum() to n; otherwise SetMinSum reverts.

For any call to Collect that succeeds, if the call executes without reverting, the stored MinSum value must be unchanged because SetMinSum was never called; the reference contract preserves the invariant that MinSum remains its initial value (0 or whatever SetMinSum set before initialization), but the mutant's SetMinSum leaves MinSum uninitialized when called, so a prior successful SetMinSum call will have set MinSum to a non-zero value in the reference, while the mutant keeps it 0, causing the assertion on MinSum after a successful Collect to fail.
After the contract is initialized and SetMinSum is called, the value of MinSum must equal the last argument passed to SetMinSum; the mutant leaves MinSum unchanged, breaking this rule.
After initialization, calling SetMinSum then Collect via a revert-on-receive callee does not alter MinSum, but the mutant keeps the old value because SetMinSum is a no-op.

After initialization, a successful call to SetMinSum must change MinSum to the provided _val; the mutant leaves MinSum unchanged, so after SetMinSum the value of MinSum equals _val in the reference but remains 0 (or its prior value) in the mutant.

After calling SetMinSum before initialization, a subsequent successful Collect must leave MinSum equal to the argument of that last SetMinSum; the mutant violates this by leaving MinSum unchanged because SetMinSum is a no-op.
After any non-reverting call to SetMinSum, the public state variable MinSum must equal the supplied _val argument (the correct version stores it; the buggy version leaves it unchanged/zero).
After the contract is fully initialized (via Initialized()), a call to SetMinSum must not revert, and MinSum must equal the supplied _val; the buggy version leaves MinSum unchanged.
After setting MinSum via SetMinSum, the public getter MinSum() returns the value that was passed as argument; the buggy version always returns 0 because the function body is empty.
After the contract is initialized, a non-reverting call to SetMinSum changes MinSum to _val in the reference, but leaves it unchanged in the buggy version.

After any call to SetMinSum, the value of MinSum remains unchanged from before the call, because the reference contract never modifies it without reverting when initialized is false; the mutant always reverts when initialized is false except it does not, and instead executes a no-op assignment, but for any input the rule is that MinSum never changes via SetMinSum. The bug violates this by allowing SetMinSum to be called successfully without changing MinSum, which is fine, but the property that MinSum remains its initial zero value after any call to SetMinSum without a revert when initialized is false holds for the reference (it reverts) and fails for the mutant (it succeeds), so the rule is: calling SetMinSum when initialized is false always reverts.
When the contract is not initialized, calling SetMinSum must always revert; the mutant silently succeeds with a no-op assignment instead of reverting.

After calling SetMinSum when the contract is not initialized, the MinSum state variable remains at its initial value (zero), but the reference always reverts while the mutant succeeds without reverting.
When the contract is not yet initialized, calling SetMinSum must NOT revert; the reference reverts (due to require in nonReentrant_), but the mutant silently succeeds, violating this expected revert.
SetLogFile always reverts when called before initialization

After any sequence of calls, if SetLogFile has been successfully invoked on the reference contract, it must not be possible to call SetLogFile again and change the LogFile address; the bug allows reentrant modification of the LogFile address after it was already set.
